answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a bond that is locked for a fixed period before it may transact. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds, while honest agents pay only once. Reputation should accumulate slowly, like a lotus opening petal by petal, rather than being granted instantly. A transparent ledger acts as a crystal record of past behaviour, and a velvet glove of graduated limits lets new agents trade small amounts until their history earns larger trust.
